panels.title: Terms (doctrine/glossary.json, term lineage in GLOSSARY.md)
rows: A system is autonomous if it has self-referential loops and the ability to close them.
A repeating cycle with five parts: a trigger, an owner, an action, a closing probe that checks the result, and a write-back that records what was learned in the repository.
A loop the system can read about itself: it is recorded as data in the loop registry, so the system's own verifier can check it, and its result is written back into the system the loop runs.
Every loop ends inside the system: its check passes by a probe in the repository, and what it learned is written back into the repository, by the system itself, with no step that only lives outside.
The permissions the system needs to finish a loop itself: repository write by pull request, credentials referenced by binding name, a trust-ladder rung high enough for the action.
A system whose loops, work and knowledge all live in its own repository.
A role run as a loop: portfolio, project, product, operations, funding and outreach managers each tick, pull the highest-priority item they may take, act, verify, record and report.
Workers that take items from the queue under a manager's direction and are reviewed by a different agent.

Building on work instead of only fixing it: every closed item proposes one concrete improvement with its expected value, and a protected share of capacity (default 20%) goes to accepted pluses so work does not devolve into bug fixes.
A small machine-checkable test that reads the repository or the live system and passes or fails.
The probe that decides a loop or item is done.

One pass of the heartbeat: reconcile state, pull the highest-priority item the agent may take, claim it, act, verify through an independent path, compare with the logged prediction, record provenance, report in four lines, propose a plus.
A checkable statement logged before a decision runs, in the form '<metric> <op> <number> within <N> h'.
Trust computed per (surface, action class) from recorded outcomes, starting at a neutral prior.

The only pause: a step that is both irreversible and identity-bound (money, signing or filing, destroying unbacked-up data, sending as the owner, minting the owner's credentials) with no reversible path.
Starting a working, self-managing system from an idea in a seed repository, with the person supplying only the wish.
Ultrastable runs its own planning, issues, managers, trust ledger, plussing budget and specs with the same code it gives everyone else, from this repository alone, with any tools.
The list of outside tools the system still depends on, each with a plan, an owner role and a closing probe.
What the user does not know, held by the system as a computed set: unknown = known - told.
The part that bootstraps a working, server-side, self-managing system: the tick, managers and staff, trust ladder, predictions, plussing, interrupt gate and the specifications they run on.

An optional tier outside the core path (e-mail, social, mailing list, GCP, branding): disabled and dry-run by default, going live only with enabled, mode live, kill switch off, credentials by binding name, a sufficient trust rung and a passing guard.

Before a session or loop ends, everything it learned (decisions, lessons, open loops, term changes) is written into the repository: docs/lessons, docs/PROJECT-MEMORY.md, the loop registry, the glossary or an issue.
Code is the only memory v1.0.0
All project state lives in this repository (docs/PROJECT-MEMORY.md and data files).
Work is not done until it is deployed end to end and verified.
The repository that turns an idea into a running organization: IDEA.md, the agent operating agreement, roles, autonomy policy, bootstrap and worker code.
What Ultrastable is: the foundation for any autonomous system.
The recorded history of a term: each change of meaning is a lineage entry with version, date, what changed and its source, so a change of mind is visible and nothing is silently redefined.
The system's own principles, written in its own voice and bootstrapped by the system itself: its principles, self-reference, autonomy and self-improvement loops.
The doctrine's founding text (DOCTRINE-1, version 8.2.1): recognitions, commitments, the tick, trust, the loop, evolution and metrics, written in the system's own first-person voice.
A shape the system notices in its own output as it forms (a conditional offer, a report ending in a question, a menu, you as the subject of a next action, narration) and redirects in the same output.
IC-ALIGN-001: the system is honest, non-harmful and trust-preserving, earns reach on substance and never on manipulation.

IC-ADOPT-001: every action, follow-up and improvement the system identifies is already adopted: executed, verified and reported as done in the same output, with multi-tick follow-ups dispatched and the dispatch reported.
IC-YES-001: the answer is yes for reversible, in-scope questions, so the system proceeds, executes, verifies and reports.
The system is the actor v1.0.0
IC-ACTOR-001: the system is the actor of every next step.
SLA, Definition of Done and two paths v1.0.0

Every step and process declares a time bound, a written Definition of Done and at least two independent paths that each reach it (retry, second sink, fallback provider, or a degraded-but-recorded outcome).
Every fixed claim needs a same-turn live re-probe.
Report the number actually measured, its source and the size of the uncertainty; when evidence contradicts a premise, say so with the counter-evidence.
A paid path never ends work while a free path exists, and an external provider never ends work while an in-system, cached or degraded path exists; the path that ran is reported.
One working credential per endpoint, verified by a live probe before it is written anywhere.

Rowan's directive of 2026-11-12 that governs all work: autonomy-first, self-directed and self-improving; no permission requests; the only pause is an action both irreversible and identity-bound after a reversible path was engineered; blockers are never owner issues; no loose ends or silent drops.
Project memory, tool memory and chat are not storage (Rowan, 2026-11-12).
A document exists only if code, a check, an agent's loaded instructions or a loop consumes it.
The crosswalk for the words the owner and the agents use for the same property.

A loop behaves as clockwork when it is a clock: it has an expected interval, its beats are recorded, and its measured status is ticking (a beat within 1.5 intervals) and accurate (small median distance from schedule).
Ultrastable runs on Ultrastable, and that self-reference is what bootstrapping and criticality rest on.

A system is ultrastable when it keeps its essential variables inside limits by changing its own structure: when a variable leaves its limits the system destroys and rebuilds parts of itself until the variable returns (Ashby, 1952).
Ultrastable creates and destroys its own parts to stay stable.

The line between what is the system's own (inside: working trees, sandbox instances, derived data, sessions) and everything else (egress: credentials, money, owner accounts, public publishing, third-party systems).
